newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish rate rise more likely on budget gap - c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Polish rate rise more likely on budget gap - c.bank.

text.p: Polish central bank head Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz told the Gazeta Wyborcza daily that next year's forecast budget deficit of 1.9 percent, makes an interest rate rise more likely to cool domestic demand.
"(Because of the size of the deficit) The earlier announced possiblity of an interest rate rise becomes more real," Hanna Gronkiewicz Waltz told the paper.
She said that domestic demand, which fuels imports, was expected to increase and dangerously widen Poland's trade gap.
"With the assumed budget deficit, the trade gap next year may reach even $16 billion," Gronkiewicz-Waltz was quoted as saying.
She said such a trade deficit could lead to a one-off devaluation of the zloty which, in turn, would speed up price growth.

The paper quoted Gronkiewicz-Waltz as saying that from the point of view of Poland's trade balance, the safe level of budget deficit for next year was just 1.5 percent of Gross Domestic Product -- on the assumption that the 1999 budget would be balanced.
"Like any other economy we cannot afford to have such a huge trade deficit, because in two years at the latest we would have serious economic problems," Gronkiewicz-Waltz said.
Last week the central bank's deputy president Witold Kozinski said that unless the 1998 budget was balanced, Poland could face a Czech-style currency crisis because of the growing trade gap.
